subject: Corelytics escalation: sustained throughput & error-rate impact — remediation package and reconciliation
messages:
From: Alice Nguyen <alice@corelytics.io>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: ben.rosario@corelytics.io
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production service disruption — throughput drop and 5xx surge (Corelytics)

Sergio,

We saw a sustained throughput regression and elevated 5xx rates starting ~02:40 PT this morning. Overall latency has increased ~2.6x for our peak traffic windows and we observed numerous request timeouts that caused downstream retries on our side. This is material for our production workload — it impacted several jobs and increased our processing backlog.

We need:
- A summary of what happened and timeline
- Initial remediation and fallback steps you can take immediately
- A preliminary calculation of credits given this appears to breach our SLA for March

Attaching a short sample of logs and a brief cluster timeline. Please escalate to your ops leadership — we're scheduling an exec sync for tomorrow if needed.

Thanks,
Alice Nguyen
Head of Platform Engineering
Corelytics Inc.

Attachments: corelytics_latency_snapshot_0301.txt (log snippet)
From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@corelytics.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, aisha_rahman@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production service disruption — throughput drop and 5xx surge (Corelytics)

Alice — thanks for the heads up and the log snippet. Sorry for the disruption; I appreciate the clear details.

Quick update / next steps:
1) Immediate mitigation: We've enabled a higher-priority routing tier for your tenant and temporarily increased reserved throughput on the affected pools. That will reduce tail latency while we investigate.
2) Investigation: Our infra team is doing a root-cause analysis; early signs point to a misapplied autoscaler policy in one of the GPU pools that caused sustained queuing under the traffic pattern you sent. We should have a more concrete RCA within 24 hours.
3) Credits: Preliminary estimate based on our SLA formula and your traffic ingestion is ~8-12% of March hosted usage as a service credit. That's a placeholder until we reconcile logs and confirm the exact outage window.
4) Exec call: I propose a 30-minute sync tomorrow (Tue 03/02) at 10:00 PT with my ops lead (Aisha) and Marissa (your AE) to walk through the remediation and next steps.

I'll attach the provisional credit worksheet and the logs we pulled on our side once we complete the collection. We're prioritizing you and will follow up with confirmed numbers and an RCA.

— Sergio Alvarez
Account Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

On Mon, Mar 1, 2027 at 09:12 AM Alice Nguyen <alice@corelytics.io> wrote:
> Sergio,
>
> We saw a sustained throughput regression and elevated 5xx rates starting ~02:40 PT this morning...
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com, aisha_rahman@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 08:13:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Production service disruption — Corelytics — proposed remediation & credit outline

Folks — looping you in ahead of the 10:00 PT exec sync. Marion (CS) will be on the call from Corelytics; Ben Rosario is their CTO and should join if schedules allow. High-level ask from Corelytics = clear RCA + expedited credit and a remediation plan that prevents recurrence.

A few notes for the call and what I want to align on beforehand:
- Credit calculation: We need a defensible recon side-by-side using their ingestion metrics and our token counts. See attached sla_credit_calc_v1.xlsx for the working model.
- Commercial remediation options: propose a blended package: 1) immediate service credit (applied to next invoice), 2) three months of prioritized capacity at a discounted rate, 3) a technical runbook & workshop to tune autoscaling for their traffic profile.
- Contract implications: if credits exceed a material threshold, legal will require an amendment. Let's not promise clause-level concessions on the call.

Aisha — can you validate the RCA hypothesis ahead of the call and outline remediation steps we can offer within 48 hours? Vivek — if this moves into a credit >10% ask we should be prepared to escalate commercially; please be on standby.

Attached: sla_credit_calc_v1.xlsx (worksheet), corelytics_latency_log_0301.zip (internal pull)

Thanks — Marissa
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sla_credit_calc_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), corelytics_latency_log_0301.zip (log archive)
From: Alice Nguyen <alice@corelytics.io>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, aisha_rahman@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production service disruption — Corelytics — proposed remediation & credit outline

Thanks for the rapid response and for prioritizing this. The provisional credit range (8-12%) sounds reasonable as a starting point; we'll reserve final judgement pending your RCA and the exact outage timing.

Agree with the blended remediation package — the prioritized capacity and the runbook workshop are particularly important for us. For the exec sync earlier today the team appreciated the transparency; Ben will review the worksheet and follow up with a single number by EOD Friday.

Please include the final credit calculation as a line item in the HubSpot deal record and share any proposed contract amendment language for legal review once you have a final number. We'll need a DocuSign path if the adjustment requires signature.

Regards,
Alice
Head of Platform Engineering
Corelytics Inc.
